• Yeah, 100%. Mirroring is currently a pain
  because the tool makes you manage
  implementation details:
  - It silently derives the plane from each
    active part’s bounds.
  - It mirrors parts independently instead of
    using one shared plane.
  - Center-crossing faces get duplicated.
  - You must manually merge faces and weld/
    clean the seam afterward.
  The proper workflow should be: choose plane
  → choose kept side → preview → apply. Apply
  should split crossing faces, mirror the
  source side, weld the centerline, merge
  compatible faces, and preserve Outliner/
  semantic ownership in one undo step.
  Also, I removed my provisional edit. Your
  model is back at the demonstrated 556
  triangles and 11 intersections; no
  attempted mirror remains.

events.text: Traced every mirror plane consumer: live mirror twin table + transform reflect (mesh_edit.zig), symmetrize/symmetrizeParts (indexed_edit_mesh.zig), symmetry report, plane overlay, diagonal sync — all derived planes from mesh/part/scope bounds. Mirror Part duplicate alone already used the origin. Unified all on mesh_edit.MIRROR_PLANE_CENTER (model origin), added same-part-first/any-part twin pairing, discovered and fixed that gpu/mesh_edit.zig's 52 inline tests never ran (no addTest root). 151/151 mesh tests pass, ReleaseFast editor compiles.

resolution: Fixed the mirror plane authority end to end. The disease behind the chair-arm log: three mirror features used three different bounds-derived planes (Mirror Edit = per-part bounds center rebuilt per transform, symmetrize = part bounds midpoint, un-parted symmetrize = scope bounds), so the first one-sided edit moved the very plane symmetry depended on. Now one fixed authority — mesh_edit.MIRROR_PLANE_CENTER at the model origin, the plane Mirror Part already reflected across and the Center button (req_1538) aligns to — is injected into live mirror twinning, symmetrize, the symmetry report, the overlay, and indexed diagonal sync. Twin pairing now falls back across outliner parts so a mirror-duplicated part follows its twin part live. Also found gpu/mesh_edit.zig's inline tests (incl. every old mirror test) never executed — module-boundary tests need their own addTest root; wired mesh-edit-impl-test into test-mesh-edit. New regression tests pin the contract: one-sided geometry cannot drift the plane, off-origin parts don't self-mirror, cross-part pairing works. 151/151 tests pass; ReleaseFast editor rebuilt. NOT yet built: true bilateral topology (extrude-both-sides under live mirror) — region extrude uses one aggregate normal so a face+twin selection cancels to zero; that needs its own design.
